faq.title: Frequently asked questions

q1.q: Do I need a residence permit to live in Istanbul?
q1.a: Yes. To stay legally beyond your visa or visa-free period you need a residence permit (İkamet). The most common first permit is the short-term one, usually valid for 1–2 years. Start by getting a tax number and mandatory health insurance, then apply on the e-İkamet portal.

q2.q: How do I open a bank account as a foreigner?
q2.a: You generally need your passport, a Turkish tax number (Vergi No), and proof of address. Requirements vary by bank and even by branch — if one refuses, another may accept you. Your card usually arrives by courier within a week.

q3.q: What is a Vergi No and how do I get one?
q3.a: It is your Turkish tax number, required for banking, rentals and most official steps. It is free and takes minutes online via the İnteraktif Vergi Dairesi portal, or about an hour at any tax office.

q4.q: Is it true some Istanbul districts are closed to new residents?
q4.a: Yes. A number of Istanbul districts are closed to new residence-permit registrations at any given time. Always verify your specific district is open BEFORE signing a rental contract, or your application can be rejected.

q5.q: Can I get Turkish citizenship by buying property?
q5.a: Property investment can make you eligible to apply for citizenship — it does not guarantee approval. You must buy above the official threshold and hold the property for three years; the final decision belongs solely to the Turkish government after its own review. Listings marked “Meets citizenship threshold” satisfy the investment amount, and our legal team verifies every title deed, but no purchase can promise citizenship itself.

q6.q: How does the free expert appointment work?
q6.a: When the AI assistant sees that your case needs a human, it offers a free online appointment (call or video). You only pick a date, time and language — your problem summary and chat are attached automatically for the specialist.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions about Referrals & Wallet
faq.q1: What is the exact commission rate?
faq.a1: The commission is a flat 5% on the net paid value of any completed service transaction originating from your referral link.
faq.q2: When is the commission credited to my wallet?
faq.a2: Commissions appear immediately upon successful payment confirmation by our billing system.
faq.a3: Commissions are recorded in the exact currency of the transaction (USD, EUR, or TRY) to prevent currency conversion losses.
faq.q4: How do I withdraw my earnings?
faq.a4: Navigate to the Wallet page, click 'Request Payout', and submit your IBAN or crypto address for manual review and transfer within 24-48 hours.
faq.q5: Is there any cap on how much I can earn?
faq.a5: No, there is no maximum limit. You earn 5% on every paid, successful transaction with no cap.
faq.q6: What happens if a transaction is refunded?
faq.a6: If a customer receives a verified refund, an offsetting reversal entry is recorded in your ledger to maintain accurate balances.

terms.title: Referral Program Terms & Guidelines
terms.body:
• The 5% commission is payable strictly on verified, paid transactions.
• Free requests, cancellations, and unpaid consultations do not generate commissions.
• Self-referrals and fraudulent accounts are strictly prohibited and subject to forfeiture.
• Payouts are processed by our finance team within 24-48 business hours.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.body:
Welcome to Rafiq Istanbul. By creating an account or using our website and services, you agree to these Terms.

1. Who we are. Rafiq Istanbul is an independent guidance and concierge service that helps foreigners settle in Istanbul. We are not a government agency, a law firm, or an official authority, and we do not issue any official document. Government fees and timelines are set by the relevant authorities, not by us.

2. Your account. You are responsible for the accuracy of the information you provide and for keeping your login credentials secure. You must be at least 18 years old to purchase a subscription.

3. Subscriptions and billing. Paid plans are billed in advance for the chosen period (monthly or annual) and renew automatically until you cancel. You can cancel at any time from the Pricing page; your access continues until the end of the period already paid.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy (KVKK)
privacy.body:
This Privacy Policy explains how Rafiq Istanbul collects and uses your information, in line with the Turkish Personal Data Protection Law (KVKK No. 6698).

1. Data we collect. Account details (name, email), the answers you give during onboarding, your service requests and bookings, documents you choose to upload, and basic usage data needed to operate the service.

2. Why we use it. To provide and personalize our services, prepare and follow up your requests, communicate with you, and improve the platform. We do not sell your personal data.

3. Sharing. We share only what is necessary with the vetted partner handling your specific request (for example, a translation office or insurance provider). Our infrastructure is hosted on secure cloud providers.

4. Storage and security. Your data is stored on protected servers with access controls. Uploaded documents stay private to your account and are accessible to our team only to deliver the service you requested.

5. Your rights (KVKK). You may request access to, correction of, or deletion of your personal data, and you may withdraw consent at any time, by contacting us.

6. Retention. We keep your data only as long as needed to provide the service and meet legal obligations, then delete or anonymize it.

7. Contact. For privacy requests, contact our team through the app.

refund.body:
Last updated: 2026-07-21

1. Scope
This policy applies to all paid services offered through the Rafiq Istanbul platform, including residence permits, tax number, banking, housing, health, and education services.

2. Government Fees
All fees paid directly to government authorities or official institutions (e.g., Immigration Office, Tax Department) are non-refundable once the application has been submitted to the relevant authority.

3. Rafiq Istanbul Service Fees
Mediation and service fees are refundable according to the following schedule:

5. Refund Request

6. Non-eligible Refunds

edevlet.title: e-Devlet — the master key
edevlet.body: Turkey's official government app. With your foreigner ID (Yabancı Kimlik No) you can view your residence permit, book appointments, download official documents, check your address registration and more — all in one place.
steps: Get your Foreigner Identification Number (Yabancı Kimlik Numarası) — it's assigned once your residence permit application is registered.
Visit any PTT (post office) branch in person with your passport and residence paperwork.
Ask for an "e-Devlet şifresi" (e-Devlet password) — it's issued on paper on the spot.
Log in at turkiye.gov.tr with your ID number and password to activate your account.
edevlet.benefit: One login for tracking your residence permit, tax records, address registration, health appointments and dozens of other official services — most available with an in-site translation into your language.

eikamet.title: e-İkamet (Göç İdaresi)
eikamet.body: The migration office portal: apply for or extend your residence permit, book your appointment, and track your card. Always verify your district is open before applying.
steps: Get your tax number and mandatory health insurance ready first — the form asks for both.
Fill in the application at e-ikamet.goc.gov.tr with your address and passport details.
Pick the earliest available appointment slot at your local migration office.
Attend with your documents; your card status can then be tracked from the same portal.
eikamet.benefit: You control your own residence-permit timeline online instead of relying on a third party, and you can watch your card's status change from application to delivery.

istanbulkart.title: Istanbulkart app
istanbulkart.body: Top up your transport card straight from your phone — no kiosk needed. It also shows your balance and the nearest ferry, metro and bus lines.
steps: Download the official İstanbulkart app for your phone.
Turn on NFC in your phone's settings and register your physical card in the app.
Add balance in-app using a bank card.
Hold your physical card against the back of your phone to transfer the new balance onto it.
istanbulkart.benefit: No more searching for a working kiosk or carrying exact change — top up anywhere, any time, and see your balance and the nearest transport lines from the same app.

bitaksi.title: BiTaksi / iTaksi
bitaksi.body: Hail a licensed, metered taxi from the app so you always pay the real fare. The trip and driver are logged — far safer than flagging one on the street.
steps: Install BiTaksi or iTaksi and set your pickup location.
Confirm the driver and plate number shown in the app before boarding.
Watch the metered fare update live during the ride.
Pay in-app or in cash for the exact metered amount shown.
bitaksi.benefit: A traceable trip with a real metered fare, instead of negotiating a flat price with a stranger on the street.

getir.title: Getir & Yemeksepeti
getir.body: Groceries in minutes and food delivery from almost anywhere. Pay by card in-app — handy before your Turkish bank account is ready.
steps: Download the app and set your delivery address.
Browse nearby restaurants or the grocery catalog and add items to your cart.
Pay with an international card if your Turkish account isn't ready yet.
Track your courier live on the map until they arrive.
getir.benefit: Groceries and meals delivered fast without needing cash or a Turkish bank account on day one.

esim.title: Buy an eSIM before you land
esim.body: An eSIM bought online is far cheaper than SIM cards sold at the airport, and you arrive already connected to book taxis and find your way.
steps: Check your phone supports eSIM (most phones released since around 2020 do).
Buy a Turkish data eSIM from a reputable provider's app or website before you fly.
Follow the QR code or activation link the provider emails you to install the eSIM profile.
After landing, turn on data roaming for the new eSIM line and you're online immediately.
esim.benefit: You arrive already connected — book a taxi, use maps and translate on the spot — and skip the queue at the airport SIM counter entirely.

vergi.title: Get your Vergi No online first
vergi.body: Your tax number is free from the İnteraktif Vergi Dairesi portal in minutes. Get it before the bank visit — most branches ask for it.
steps: Go to the İnteraktif Vergi Dairesi website (gib.gov.tr).
Choose the foreign-national tax number application option.
Enter your passport details and upload your passport photo page.
Receive your number instantly online, or get it in person at any Vergi Dairesi with your passport.
vergi.benefit: A free tax number in minutes — required for renting a home, opening a bank account and applying for your residence permit.

taxiCaution.title: Never ride an unmetered taxi
taxiCaution.body: Insist on the meter ("taksimetre") or use a taxi app. Agreeing a price by hand on day one is the most common way newcomers overpay.
steps: Ask the driver to switch on the "taksimetre" (meter) before the car moves.
Prefer app-based rides (BiTaksi, iTaksi, Uber), where the fare, driver and route are all logged.
If a driver refuses the meter or names a flat price, step out and take a different taxi.
Keep the receipt or the app's trip summary until you reach your destination.
taxiCaution.benefit: You pay the real metered fare instead of an inflated "tourist price," with a digital record if a dispute ever comes up.

istanbulkartTopup.title: Top up İstanbulkart from your phone
istanbulkartTopup.body: Skip the kiosk queue: recharge your transport card straight from your phone, anywhere, any time.
steps: Download the official İstanbulkart app matching your phone's operating system.
Enable NFC in your phone's settings and register your physical card inside the app.
Load balance onto the app using a bank card.
Tap your physical card against your phone's NFC reader to transfer the new balance.
istanbulkartTopup.benefit: No more hunting for a working kiosk or carrying exact change — top up anywhere, and check your balance plus the nearest bus, metro and ferry lines in the same app.

imeiRegistration.title: Register your foreign phone before day 120
imeiRegistration.body: Planning to keep using a Turkish SIM in a phone you brought from abroad past the first few months? Register it early — the clock starts from your first local SIM use.
steps: Confirm you hold a Foreigner Identification Number (YKN) and an active e-Devlet login.
Log in to e-Devlet and open the mobile phone (IMEI) registration service.
Find your phone's IMEI by dialing *#06# on the handset, then enter it in the form.
Complete the registration before your 120th day of using a Turkish SIM in that phone, or the network blocks the device.
imeiRegistration.benefit: Your own phone keeps working on a Turkish number for the long term, instead of being locked out of local networks once the grace period ends.

moneyExchange.title: Exchange money the safe way
moneyExchange.body: Skip hotel counters and airport booths — a little homework before you exchange cash keeps more of it in your pocket.
steps: Compare the buy/sell rate board at a few licensed exchange offices ("döviz") in the city center rather than the first one you see.
Avoid exchanging at airports, hotels or street touts — their posted rates are consistently worse than city-center offices.
Count your cash at the counter before you walk away, and ask for a receipt.
For larger amounts, compare against your own bank card's conversion rate — sometimes an ATM withdrawal works out better.
moneyExchange.benefit: You keep more of your money instead of losing a chunk of it to inflated tourist-zone exchange rates.

freeWifi.title: Use free municipal Wi-Fi (İBB WiFi)
freeWifi.body: Istanbul's metropolitan municipality runs a free public Wi-Fi network across parks, squares, metro stations and ferries.
steps: Look for the "İBB WiFi" network in the list of available Wi-Fi networks in public areas.
Connect to it and open any browser — you'll be redirected to a registration page.
Verify with your phone number (an SMS code is sent) to unlock free access.
freeWifi.benefit: Free internet in most public spaces around the city — handy for maps and messaging while you top up your own data plan.

marmaray.title: Cross continents on the Marmaray
marmaray.body: The Marmaray rail line runs under the Bosphorus, linking the European and Asian sides of the city in one uninterrupted ride.
steps: Tap in with your İstanbulkart at any Marmaray station along the Halkalı–Gebze line.
Ride straight under the strait — no ferry, traffic or bridge crossing needed.
Transfer to metro or bus lines at major interchange stations like Üsküdar, Sirkeci or Ayrılık Çeşmesi.
marmaray.benefit: A fast, weatherproof way to cross between Europe and Asia at any hour, skipping bridge traffic and ferry schedules entirely.

museumPass.title: Skip museum lines with the Museum Pass
museumPass.body: A single pass gives timed, one-time entry to a wide list of Istanbul's major museums and palaces across several consecutive days.
steps: Buy the Museum Pass Istanbul online or at a participating museum before your first visit.
Its validity window starts the moment you use it for the first time, so time your purchase accordingly.
Visit any of the included museums and palaces once each within that validity window.
Go straight to the entrance with your pass instead of queueing at the standalone ticket counter.
museumPass.benefit: You avoid the ticket line at popular sites like Topkapı Palace, and one pass replaces many separate admission tickets during your stay.

dolmus.title: Ride a dolmuş like a local
dolmus.body: Dolmuş are shared minibuses running fixed routes, filling up before they leave and dropping passengers off anywhere along the way.
steps: Find the route board on the minibus windshield showing its start and end points.
Flag it down anywhere along its route, or wait at a recognized dolmuş stop.
Pay the driver in cash as you board, or pass your fare forward through other passengers if you're seated further back.
Call out "inecek var" (someone's getting off) when you want the driver to stop.
dolmus.benefit: You reach routes and neighborhoods that regular buses or metro lines don't cover directly, often faster than waiting for a full-size bus.

addressRegistration.title: Register your address before your residence appointment
addressRegistration.body: Your address record has to match your paperwork before the migration office will approve your residence permit application.
steps: Sign a rental contract for your address, ideally notarized or through a registered agent.
Ask your landlord or building manager to confirm the address matches official building records.
Update your registered address on e-Devlet once everything lines up.
Only then submit or continue your residence permit (e-İkamet) application using that address.
addressRegistration.benefit: You avoid the single most common rejection reason for residence-permit applications — an address record that doesn't match your file.
